question: Should ClawHub add a standard SKILL.md capability manifest for network, filesystem, external-code execution, and secret-reading boundaries, and what schema, rollout policy, and authority model should it use?
rationale: This changes the skill trust boundary and reviewer contract; automation cannot safely choose the taxonomy, advisory-versus-required timeline, or self-declared versus verified semantics without maintainer security/product intent.

options.title: Adopt a spec-backed advisory manifest
options.body: Define the capability schema and authority model in specs first, then ship parser/API/docs and advisory declared-vs-observed review output before making it required.

options.title: Defer to scanner-only review
options.body: Keep using ClawScan and static signals without adding author-declared capability metadata, avoiding new schema surface but leaving reviewers without an author-declared baseline.

options.title: Revive the old PR shape after redesign
options.body: Use the closed capability-manifest PR as implementation reference only after fixing its parsing/API concerns and aligning the taxonomy with this RFC.

recommendation.title: Adopt a spec-backed advisory manifest
recommendation.body: Define the capability schema and authority model in specs first, then ship parser/API/docs and advisory declared-vs-observed review output before making it required.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS and blame connect this handle to the security-sensitive schema, moderation, and security prompt surfaces most affected by the decision.
